questions.question:
List all the **worker** nodes in the cluster and write their names to the file `/tmp/exam/nodes.txt` (one node name per line).

The control-plane (server) node must **not** be included in the file.

verification.description: Output file /tmp/exam/nodes.txt exists and is not empty
All worker nodes are listed in the file
Control-plane node is excluded from the file

questions.question:
In the namespace `pod-basics`, create `3` pods named `web-1`, `web-2` and `web-3` using the `busybox:1.36` image.

Each pod must run the command `sleep 3600` and carry the label `app=web`.

Once all 3 pods are running, write the names of the running pods (one per line) to the file `/tmp/exam/running-pods.txt`.

verification.description: All pods are in Running state
Running pod names are listed in /tmp/exam/running-pods.txt

questions.question:
Label the node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` with `disk=ssd`.

Then, in the namespace `node-select`, create a pod named `nginx-pod` using the `nginx:1.27` image that is scheduled **only** on that node using a `nodeSelector`.

verification.description: Pod nginx-pod exists with nodeSelector disk=ssd

questions.question:
In the namespace `nodeport-lab`:

1. Create a deployment named `web-app` with `2` replicas using the `nginx:1.27` image. The pods must carry the label `app=web-app`.
2. Expose it through a service named `web-svc` of type `NodePort` that listens on port `80` and maps to NodePort `30088`.

verification.description: Deployment web-app exists with 2 ready replicas
Service web-svc is NodePort exposing port 80

questions.question:
The deployment `web-recovery` in namespace `image-fix` was deployed with an incorrect image tag (`nginx:1.25.12-typo`) and its pods are stuck in `ImagePullBackOff`.

Fix the deployment so that all its pods are running and ready. Do **not** delete and recreate the deployment - repair it in place.

verification.description: Deployment no longer uses the broken image
All pods are Running with no pull errors

questions.question:
In the namespace `batch-jobs`, create a job named `batch-worker` using the `busybox:1.36` image.

The job must run the command `echo processing && sleep 5` and meet these requirements:

1. Run `4` pods to completion (`completions`)
2. Allow `2` pods to run in parallel (`parallelism`)
3. Use a `backoffLimit` of `6`
4. Set `restartPolicy` to `Never`
5. Clean itself up `120` seconds after finishing (`ttlSecondsAfterFinished`)

A certificate signing request named `app-web-csr` is waiting for manual approval in the cluster.

Approve the CSR so that it shows an `Approved` condition. Do not deny it and do not delete and recreate it.

The persistent volume claim `data-pvc` in namespace `storage-expand` was created with a request of `2Gi` and needs more space.

1. Ensure the storage class `expandable` has `allowVolumeExpansion` enabled
2. Expand `data-pvc` to request `5Gi` without recreating it. The claim must stay `Bound`.

The service `frontend-svc` in namespace `svc-endpoints` has no endpoints even though the `frontend` deployment is running with 2 ready pods.

Find the misconfiguration and fix the service so that traffic actually reaches the pods. Do not delete and recreate the deployment.

verification.description: Service selector matches the pod label app=frontend

questions.question:
In namespace `netpol-debug`, the service `backend` routes to pods that the network policy `backend-access` is supposed to protect: traffic on port `80` must only be allowed from pods labeled `access=granted`.

Because of a misconfiguration, **no pod can currently reach the backend**. The policy mistakenly selects pods labeled `app=frontend`, which do not exist.

Fix the policy so that:

1. Pods labeled `access=granted` (like the `tester` pod) can reach the backend on port `80`
2. The policy still only protects the `backend` pods on port 80

verification.description: Policy allows from pods labeled access=granted
Policy still targets backend pods on port 80
Tester pod can actually reach the backend

questions.question:
The pod `app-crasher` in namespace `debug-pod` is running but never becomes `Ready` - it stays `0/1`.

The app container keeps waiting for a configuration file that does not exist, and its readiness probe only passes once the file `/app/config/settings.conf` is present.

1. Use `kubectl debug` to attach an **ephemeral container** to `app-crasher` and investigate why the pod is not ready
2. Using your findings, create the missing file so that the pod reaches `Ready` (the file must exist inside the app container at `/app/config/settings.conf`)

verification.description: An ephemeral container was added to app-crasher

questions.question:
Three manifest files in the directory `/tmp/exam/deprecations/` use **deprecated API versions** that have been removed from the cluster and can no longer be applied:

- `deployment.yaml` (apps/v1beta2)
- `ingress.yaml` (extensions/v1beta1)
- `cronjob.yaml` (batch/v1beta1)

Update each manifest to its current API version - adding any fields the new version requires (for example `pathType` on the ingress and the nested `jobTemplate.spec.template.spec` structure on the cronjob) - and apply all three resources to the namespace `api-update`.

verification.description: Deployment uses apps/v1 and is applied
Ingress uses networking.k8s.io/v1 with valid fields
CronJob uses batch/v1 with correct schedule

questions.question:
In namespace `rbac-debug`, the service account `pod-viewer` is bound to the role `pod-inspector`. It can list pods, but the application using it receives a `403 Forbidden` when it tries to read configmaps (for example `app-settings`).

Find the missing permission and grant it so the service account can `get` configmaps in its namespace.

Keep the fix **scoped**: the service account must not gain access to other namespaces or cluster-wide permissions.

In the namespace `spread`, create a deployment named `spread-app` with `4` replicas using the `nginx:1.27` image. The pods must carry the label `app=spread-app`.

The replicas must be spread evenly across the worker nodes:

1. Add a `topologySpreadConstraints` entry with `topologyKey` set to `kubernetes.io/hostname`
2. Set `maxSkew` to `1`
3. Set `whenUnsatisfiable` to `DoNotSchedule`
4. Match the constraint to the pod label `app=spread-app`

verification.description: Pods are evenly distributed across nodes

questions.question:
The application in namespace `repair` is broken in multiple ways. The deployment `shop` shows pods that never become ready, and the service `shop-svc` routes no traffic despite the pods existing.

There are **three** separate faults to find and fix:

1. The deployment's readiness probe checks a path that does not exist, so the pods never report Ready
2. The service selector does not match the pods' labels
3. The service `targetPort` does not match the port the container listens on

Repair all three so that all `3` replicas are ready and traffic flows through `shop-svc`.

verification.description: Service selector and targetPort are correct

questions.question:
Node `k3d-cluster-agent-1` was taken offline for maintenance: it was cordoned and tainted with `dedicated=critical:NoSchedule`.

The deployment `critical-app` in namespace `maintenance` targets this node and its 3 pods are stuck `Pending`, leaving the application down.

Restore the service:

1. Make the node schedulable again (uncordon it)
2. Remove the `dedicated=critical` taint from the node
3. Bring the `critical-app` deployment back to 3 running replicas on that node

verification.description: All critical-app pods run on k3d-cluster-agent-1
